uncited: *   **Inputs:** A rendered image $I_j$ from the current view and a warped pseudo-ground-truth image $I_{i \to j}$ derived from a reference view $I_i$ using estimated depth and camera geometry.
*   **Feature Maps:** Multi-level feature maps $f_{\phi_l}(I)$ extracted from a convolutional network $f_\phi$.
*   **Number of Levels ($L$):** The number of convolutional layers used for consistency checking.
**Warping (Preprocessing):** Generate the warped image $I_{i \to j}$ from source view $I_i$ using rendered depth $D_j$ and camera transformation $R_{j \to i}$.
The total Multi-level Semantic Consistency Loss integrates this with pixel-level loss.
*   **Non-Lambertian Surfaces:** Naive pixel-wise loss fails here due to view-dependent appearance changes.
*   **Self-occlusion and Artifacts:** Geometry errors can cause imperfect warping.
Multi-level Semantic Consistency Loss was introduced in the context of generalizable Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) to assist with more informative representation learning.
The approach builds on the observation that standard pixel-wise losses are insufficient for non-Lambertian scenes and leverages deep feature spaces for more stable regularization.
